title: Role of prior austenite grain size on the bainite transformation kinetics and mechanical properties of Al-containing carbide-free bainitic steel
abstract: Carbide-free bainitic (CFB) steels require achieving a balance between formability and service safety while maintaining low-alloy costs. This study reveals the critical role of austenitization temperature, through its effect on prior austenite grain size (PAGS), in controlling bainitic transformation kinetics and mechanical properties in Al-containing CFB steel by dilatometry, scanning electron microscopy, electron back-scattered diffraction, X-ray diffraction, and transmission electron microscopy. Various austenitization temperatures ranged from 850 °C to 950 °C were employed followed by austempering at 400 °C for 1 h to examine the bainitic transformation at different experimental conditions. As austenitization temperature rose from 850 °C to 950 °C, the PAGS grew from 17.2 to 46.3 μm. Refinement of PAGS significantly enhanced the nucleation site density at grain boundaries, accelerating the bainitic transformation and stabilizing the retained austenite (RA) through increased carbon partitioning. At austenitization temperatures of 900 °C and 950 °C, a significant amount of martensite and large-sized low-stability retained austenite was obtained, which deteriorated the ductility. Conversely, a lower austenitization temperature of 850 °C facilitated the formation of finer bainite and enhanced both quantity and stability of the retained austenite. A superior combination of mechanical properties was obtained, including the yield strength of 778 ± 16 MPa, the tensile strength of 1162 ± 17 MPa, and an elongation of 29.6 ± 0.9 %. The straightforward processing method, characterized by a reduced austenitization temperature followed by a single-step bainitic transformation treatment, combined with the low cost of alloying, makes the aluminum-containing CFB steel highly suitable for industrial applications.
